The quality inspector was walking from the inspection bench to the parts washer carrying a tote of samples. The task was underway because the samples were being taken for a scheduled cleanliness check. Stage of the task: walking or moving between areas. Method in effect: No written procedure exists for walking between these areas. No written procedure exists for this task. Object handled weighed approximately 15 pounds. Object size and shape: a tote about 18 by 12 by 8 inches, carried level in both arms. The object was held as follows: carried in both arms against the chest, which blocked the view of the floor ahead. PPE in use: Safety glasses and steel toe boots. This matched the PPE specified for the task. Immediately before the event: walking at normal pace along the main aisle with the tote held in both arms at chest height, looking ahead rather than down at the floor. At the moment of the event: the right foot contacted a patch of coolant on the aisle floor, the foot slid forward, balance was lost backwards, and the fall was taken onto the right hip and the outstretched right hand. Immediately after the event: the tote was dropped and the samples scattered, the inspector remained on the floor for about a minute, and a passing operator called the team lead. The quality inspector fell on the same level. Walking surface: Sealed concrete aisle floor with a patch of coolant about 18 inches across, not marked or barriered at the time. Loss of footing: the right foot slid forward on the coolant, balance was lost backwards, and the fall was taken onto the right hip and the outstretched right hand. Footwear: Site issued slip resistant safety boots, soles worn smooth at the heel. Carried at the time: A tote of samples held in both arms, obscuring the view of the floor ahead. Point of contact and direction of force: the right hip contacted the floor first with the force directed upward through the hip, followed by the outstretched right hand. Difference from a normal run of this task: The coolant patch was new. Badge 448192 reported the same leak from the adjacent machine earlier in the shift. Conditions at the point of injury: wet, oily or contaminated floor and poor or glaring lighting. Detail: The aisle light above this section has been out for about two weeks and the area is lit by spill light from the next bay. Timing: About 7 hours into a 12 hour shift and roughly 30 seconds into this walk. The quality inspector had performed this task before. A known hazard, prior near miss, open action or risk assessment covers this task. Detail: A coolant leak on the adjacent machine was raised as a near miss about two weeks ago and the corrective action to reseal the housing is still open. A guard, interlock, barrier or control was bypassed, missing, defeated or ineffective. Detail: Spill absorbent and cones are kept at the end of the aisle but the spill had not been marked or contained when it was first seen. Stop-work opportunity: The leak could have been reported and the aisle coned when it was first noticed earlier in the shift, but it was treated as a routine drip. First aid at the scene: A cold pack was applied to the right hip in the first aid room for about 15 minutes. This was given by a trained first aid responder. Notification: The team lead attended within about a minute and EHS was notified within ten minutes. Scene and equipment: The aisle was coned and the coolant was absorbed before the area was reopened. Work at the location stopped. The quality inspector was sent to an offsite occupational clinic for evaluation.
